regulatory_regime: Open-source project contribution policy (part of the LLVM developer policy)
geo_constraints: All contributions to the LLVM project and its digital spaces (GitHub, Discourse, Discord, etc.)

locale_context.regulation: Internal policy · open-source community contribution rules enforced by maintainers
locale_context.culture: Open-source community norms: protects scarce volunteer maintainer time and contributor learning, insisting on human authorship, accountability and transparency rather than banning AI tools.

versions.title: Policy text as in the asago copy (undated)
versions.summary: Only one version recorded for this policy.

covered_systems: AI agents acting in project spaces
covered_activities: comments and feedback on pull requests
exceptions: opt-in review tools that keep a human in the loop are acceptable
translation or copy-editing tools for PR descriptions
conditions: labelling applies to contributions with substantial tool-generated content
objective: Allow contributors to use AI tools while keeping a human in the loop, so that contributions are reviewed, understood and accountable and do not extract more maintainer time than they are worth.

related_policies.policy: Fedora Council policy proposal: Policy on AI-Assisted Contributions
LLVM copyright and license policy (Developer Policy)

conflict_rule: Copyright treatment follows the project's general copyright policy; enforcement is left to maintainers' judgment.

sources_consulted: http://llvm.org/docs/AIToolPolicy.html (URL printed in the policy; not fetched)
record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/llvm.md). (asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper commit b8ac8876beec6593ef5685d7d7e64cc94f9cc55b.) The document states no adoption date or version; the only date is a reference 'fetched 2025-10-01', so the version date 2025-10 is an inference (policy adopted no earlier than October 2025) and effective_date is left null. The printed official URL (llvm.org/docs/AIToolPolicy.html) is used as source_uri but was not fetched, so whether the online text has since changed is unverified. Binding=false: not law; mandatory for contributors and enforced by maintainers (request changes, 'extractive' label, escalation to moderators, removal of infringing contributions). Some text is acknowledged as copied from the Fedora policy proposal (CC BY 4.0).

clauses.original_text: Contributors must read and review all LLM-generated code or text before they ask other project members to review it. The contributor is always the author and is fully accountable for their contributions.
clauses.requirement: self-review of all LLM output before requesting review; contributor is author and accountable
clauses.purpose: quality and accountability; protect maintainer time
clauses.applicable_systems: LLMs, coding assistants, AI agents and automated review tools used for LLVM contributions
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago Markdown copy; Markdown emphasis and link syntax removed, wording unchanged. Contributors should also be able to answer questions about their work during review.

clauses.original_text: Contributors are expected to be transparent and label contributions that contain substantial amounts of tool-generated content. … Contributors should note tool usage in their pull request description, commit message, or wherever authorship is normally indicated for the work.
clauses.requirement: disclose AI tool usage, e.g. via an 'Assisted-by:' commit trailer
clauses.condition: where the contribution contains substantial amounts of tool-generated content
clauses.applicable_systems: LLMs, coding assistants, AI agents and automated review tools used for LLVM contributions
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago Markdown copy; Markdown emphasis and link syntax removed, wording unchanged. Labelling is intended to facilitate reviews, not to track which parts of LLVM are generated.

clauses.original_text: An important implication of this policy is that it bans agents that take action in our digital spaces without human approval, such as the GitHub @claude agent. Similarly, automated review tools that publish comments without human review are not allowed.
clauses.object: AI agents acting without human approval; automated review tools publishing without human review
clauses.requirement: no autonomous AI agents or unreviewed automated review comments in project spaces
clauses.exception: opt-in review tools that keep a human in the loop
clauses.purpose: keep a human in the loop
clauses.applicable_systems: AI agents and automated review tools
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago Markdown copy; Markdown emphasis and link syntax removed, wording unchanged. Opt-in review tools that keep a human in the loop are acceptable.

clauses.original_text: AI tools must not be used to fix GitHub issues labelled good first issue.
clauses.requirement: 'good first issue' tasks must be done without AI tools
clauses.purpose: preserve learning opportunities for new contributors
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago Markdown copy; Markdown emphasis and link syntax removed, wording unchanged. Restated in bold: 'Using AI tools to fix issues labelled as "good first issues" is forbidden'. Rationale is skill-building rather than output quality.

clauses.original_text: Contributors are responsible for ensuring that they have the right to contribute code under the terms of our license, typically meaning that either they, their employer, or their collaborators hold the copyright. Using AI tools to regenerate copyrighted material does not remove the copyright, and contributors are responsible for ensuring that such material does not appear in their contributions.
clauses.action: ensure rights to contribute; keep out
clauses.requirement: contributors ensure licensing rights and exclude copyrighted material reproduced by AI
clauses.applicable_systems: LLMs, coding assistants, AI agents and automated review tools used for LLVM contributions
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago Markdown copy; Markdown emphasis and link syntax removed, wording unchanged. Contributions found to violate this are removed like any other offending contribution.

clauses.original_text: If a contributor fails to make their change meaningfully less extractive, maintainers should escalate to the relevant moderation or admin team for the space (GitHub, Discourse, Discord, etc) to lock the conversation.
clauses.requirement: escalate and lock conversations where contributors do not fix extractive contributions
clauses.condition: if the contributor fails to make the change meaningfully less extractive
clauses.purpose: enforce the policy and protect maintainer time
clauses.applicable_systems: contributions in GitHub, Discourse, Discord and other project spaces
clauses.interpretation_notes: Text from the asago Markdown copy; Markdown emphasis and link syntax removed, wording unchanged. Preceded by a standard request-changes response and the 'extractive' label.
